key_insight: MLExpert pushes machine learning engineering toward a generalist autonomous agent that can plan, execute, and improve ML workflows end-to-end. It treats AI system development as an AI4AI problem, aiming to move from human-guided assistance to model-driven self-improvement.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of automating complex, long-horizon machine learning engineering tasks that require orchestration across experimentation, debugging, evaluation, and iterative refinement. Existing tools often help with isolated steps, but struggle to autonomously manage the full workflow.
method: Builds a generalist agentic model designed for autonomous machine learning engineering rather than single-task assistance.
Uses workflow-driven MLE orchestration to coordinate long-horizon experimentation and improvement loops.
Adopts model-directed interaction so the system can take actions, observe outcomes, and iteratively refine AI systems with less human intervention.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this points toward systems that can reduce manual engineering overhead and accelerate research iteration. It could make end-to-end model development, tuning, and improvement more autonomous and scalable.
visual_elements: Workflow diagram showing the loop: plan -> run experiments -> evaluate -> refine -> redeploy
Agent architecture schematic with modules for reasoning, tool use, memory, and execution
Before/after comparison of human-led MLE versus autonomous agentic MLE
Icon set representing dataset, model, experiment, metrics, and improvement cycle
paper_title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
paper_authors: Shangheng Du, Jinxin Shi, Shuaiyu Zhang, Yiming Wu, Junpeng Zhao
